text: A slouched posture makes a person look shorter and heavier.
quote: Poor posture is one of the quickest ways to ruin a pose, as it can make a subject look shorter and heavier.

text: Lifting through the top of the head and relaxing the shoulders can make the visible neck length appear nearly double compared with slouching.
quote: In the image with good posture, the length of her neck appears to nearly double.

text: Slouching makes the midsection bunch into rolls of skin or fabric across the stomach, worse on fuller-figured people; upright posture tightens it.
quote: When someone slouches, their midsection often gathers in an unflattering way, and you are likely to struggle with rolls in the fabric or skin in the stomach area.

text: A forced 'stand up straight' posture looks rigid and tense; lifting through the head with relaxed shoulders looks natural.
quote: Be wary of simply telling a subject to “stand up straight” or “sit up straight.” The results are often rigid, tense, and uncomfortable.

text: Tensed fingers and clenched hands give away nervousness or stress even when the rest of the body is posed to look relaxed.
quote: People show tension in their hands. If they are nervous, uncomfortable, or stressed, the hands will tell their secret.

text: A prominent thumb can make the hand look stumpy; keep the thumb from drawing attention.
quote: Thumbs break up the flow of a pose or can look rather stumpy, so be wary of them drawing too much attention in a hand pose.

text: People hold their tension in a clenched jaw, tight lips, raised shoulders and stiff fingers, which show as a tense body.
quote: shrug their shoulders, and wiggle their fingers around. These are the most common areas where people bottle up their tension.

text: A slightly raised shoulder reads as unrelaxed posture; lowering it makes the stance look at ease.
quote: While her posture is not terrible, her shoulder is slightly raised and could be more relaxed.

text: A figure that reads in silhouette as a boxy column with no curves will look that way in the picture; negative space and curves add feminine lines.
quote: If the body looks like a column (very boxy with no curves) in silhouette ( FIGURE 5.24 ), it will probably look that way in the shot.

text: A symmetrical, square stance reads as strong and stable and lets a person command their space, though it can look static.
quote: Symmetry conveys strength and stability, and it is a tool that a subject can use to command their space

text: Arms bent at near-right angles, such as both hands firmly on the hips, make a person look strong and stable.
quote: the near-right angles of the knee and elbow exude strength and stability, while the asymmetry of features creates visual interest

text: Contrapposto: weight on one leg with that hip popped out, the other knee bent inward and its foot lifted, shoulders tilted toward the raised hip, forms a sinuous S curve.
quote: To create contrapposto, a subject stands with most of the weight on one leg—the engaged leg—typically popping that hip out a bit.

text: Leaning back with the hips pushed far forward makes the midsection look wider; pushing hips and waist back corrects the proportion.
condition: leaning against a railing or wall
quote: Her hips are pushed far toward the camera as she leans back on the railing, making her midsection look wider.

text: A very slender man turned away looks puny; facing him straight on makes him look broader, stronger and more present.
quote: If you rotate his shoulders away from the camera, they will look even narrower. Unfortunately, this pose may make him look a bit puny

text: Turning a heavy-set man fully sideways shows his belly in profile; use only a slight angle.
quote: If you turn a heavier-set man completely to the side, it will draw more attention to problem areas by showing his midsection in profile.

text: Extremely broad shoulders can make a man's head look small and his body out of proportion.
quote: At times, a man with extremely broad shoulders may appear to have a smaller head or disproportionate body

text: A man standing straight or leaning slightly back reads as dominant and strong but pushes the belly forward; leaning forward looks slimmer and more approachable.
quote: Having your subject stand up straight or lean back slightly may visually communicate dominance and strength.

text: Unposed men default to standing flat-footed, hips square, hands in pockets or clasped together in front, which looks static.
quote: By default, men will stand flat-footed, with their hips straight toward the camera. They either put their hands in their pockets or hold their hands together in front of them.

text: A man standing square with shoulders raised high looks tense and over-posed; relaxed, lowered shoulders look natural.
quote: The subject stands square to the camera, with shoulders raised too high, creating tension and looking too posed.

text: A defined waist is seen as attractive at any size, from very slim to very full, and gives an hourglass figure.
quote: It doesn’t matter whether your subject is a size 2 or 22; a defined waist is generally considered aesthetically pleasing.

text: A body much fuller on the lower half than the top (pear shape) draws the eye to the hips, so visual weight is added up top to balance the figure.
quote: if your subject is much fuller on the bottom portion of her body than the top, you can add visual balance to the top of the image

text: When a person sits, skin and rolls gather at the midsection, more visibly on fuller figures and under form-fitting clothes.
quote: When our subjects are sitting, often the skin or rolls in their midsection gather.

text: In contrapposto the weight rests on one leg so that hip juts out, the shoulder leans toward that hip and the opposite knee bends slightly, giving an S-curve.
quote: the subject typically rests the weight on one leg so that the hip juts out slightly. The subject then leans a shoulder toward that outward hip.

text: Buttocks that look full and round read as attractive, while flat or deflated-looking buttocks do not.
quote: you want it to look full and round instead of flat or deflated

text: A twisted or bent pose can create a roll of skin in the middle of the back.
quote: The pose has created an unflattering roll of skin in the middle back.

text: Flattering posing differs by sex: women are shown with bends, curves and tapering points, men with structure and squared shoulders that show breadth.
quote: For men, create structure and position shoulders to define broadness

text: An example slender young woman is 5 ft 8 in tall and a U.S. size 0; such a body does not need slimming.
quote: When posing slender subjects (in her case, 5’8” and a size 0 in U.S. clothing), you are not trying to slenderize

text: A very slender body can read as twig-like, without flowing shape.
quote: Very slender subjects may come off as twig-like or lacking flow in their shape

text: A narrow-framed woman standing naturally looks straight and column-like, with no curves.
quote: Notice how her natural stance and narrow stature make her look very column-like

text: On a slender body an arm resting against the side does not make the figure look wide, unlike on fuller bodies.
quote: With slender subjects, I don’t worry as much about mergers, and sometimes they can actually be helpful.

text: A slouching person sinks into the shoulders, which rise and make the neck look short.
quote: The subject is slouching, essentially falling into her shoulders, which raises the shoulders and shortens the neck.

text: Real bodies may show looser skin on the arms and thighs and cellulite on the thighs, which retouching removes.
quote: Retouching has been used to lessen areas of looser skin on her arm and thigh and to remove cellulite

text: A man standing hunched and slouched reads as lacking strength and structure.
quote: Overall, the pose is hunched and lacks strength or structure.

text: A woman taller than her male partner tends to lean away to look shorter, which distorts her hips, shoulders and posture.
quote: She is taller than her husband, causing her to lean away from the camera to appear shorter. This affects her hips, shoulders, and general posture.

text: One curvy body type pairs a petite torso with very curvaceous hips and thighs.
quote: She has a petite torso and very curvaceous hips and thighs.

text: Raised shoulders show tension and shorten the neck; relaxed, lowered shoulders improve posture.
quote: Her shoulders are raised, showing tension and shortening her neck.

text: A recent rough sport such as paintball leaves visible bruises on the skin, which glossy retouched photos remove.
quote: Because she had played paintball a few days before the shoot, I’ve retouched the image using the Clone and Patch tools, to remove the bruises.
